Designers sell, subcontractors build

Beautiful renderings, but the designer hands the build off to a contractor, who hands it to subs. The people building it were never part of the design, so the details get lost.

We design it and we build it

Design, material selection, project management, demolition, carpentry, and installation are all handled by Transitions employees. The work most firms sub out, we do ourselves.

Costs creep up

Each sub prices their own piece, and the gaps between them turn into change orders. No one owns the total, so the price you were quoted isn't the price you pay.

The budget holds

Our owner, Craig, estimates every remodel himself, before you sign. Because one team owns the design and the build, the full scope is accounted for up front, so change orders are rare and the budget holds.

No one owns the outcome

When something goes wrong, it's often unclear who's responsible. The designer points to the sub, the sub points back. You're caught in the middle.

We own every outcome

From the first showroom visit to the final walkthrough, Craig stays personally involved. The result is ours, and we stand behind it.

A different crew every job

The plumber, electrician, and tile setter change from project to project. You hope for their best people and might get whoever was free that week.

The same trusted trades every time

The licensed work, plumbing, electrical, and tile, comes from the same trusted trades on every job. They've worked with us for years, they know our standard, and you have one firm to call if anything is ever off.

Inconsistent quality

What you get depends on which crew they hired that week. The renderings look the same. The finished work may not.

What happens after I fill out the form?

+

You'll be able to pick a time for your showroom visit right away. One of our designers will also follow up by email or phone to learn more about your project so we're prepared when you arrive.

Do I need an appointment?

+

Walk-ins are welcome during business hours. Scheduling ahead just means a designer will be available to give you their full attention and answer project-specific questions.

How far in advance should I start planning?

+

We recommend reaching out 2-3 months before your ideal start date. Design, material selection, and ordering take time, starting earlier means a smoother process.

Is there a fee for the initial visit?

+

No. Your first showroom visit and conversation are completely free with no obligation. We want you to feel confident before making any commitment.

What area do you serve?

+

We're based in Norwell and have been working with homeowners across the South Shore and Greater Boston since 2006.

On the South Shore, we regularly work in Hingham, Cohasset, Scituate, Marshfield, Duxbury, Kingston, Plymouth, Hanover, Pembroke, Hanson, Halifax, Rockland, Abington, Whitman, Hull, Weymouth, Braintree, Holbrook, and Quincy.

West and inland, we work in Milton, Canton, Sharon, Easton, Norton, Norfolk, Norwood, Dedham, Westwood, Needham, Wellesley, Weston, Newton, and Brookline.

For materials-only projects, our reach is even broader, we've supplied cabinetry and finishes for homes as far as Martha's Vineyard.

We work on projects of all sizes, from materials only to a full first floor remodel, and we'd rather have an honest conversation about fit than turn anyone away based on zip code or budget. If you don't see your town listed or you're nearby and not sure, give us a call. Chances are we cover it.

Do you do home additions?

+

Smaller additions and bump-outs, yes, especially when they support a kitchen or bath layout we're already remodeling. Larger additions are case-by-case, typically when paired with a broader remodel. Reach out and we'll see if it's a fit.

WHAT SETS US APART

True design‑build means one team, one vision.

Many firms say they're "design-build." We actually are. Our designers, project managers, and builders all work together in-house — so nothing gets lost in translation.

One Integrated Team

No subcontractor roulette. The people who design your kitchen are steps away from the people who build it. That means better communication, fewer mistakes, and a finished product that matches the vision.

5,000 Sq Ft Showroom

See and touch real materials before you commit. Compare countertops, cabinetry, and fixtures side by side. The South Shore’s largest kitchen and bath showroom, not a sales office with a few samples.

Expert Design Guidance

Our designers guide you through every decision, including layout, materials, finishes, and budget, so you can make confident choices. No guessing, no buyer’s remorse, and no surprise costs down the road.

Our crew has been working together for over ten years. From demo and framing to plumbing, electrical, tile, and finish carpentry, their craftsmanship is what turns designs into reality.

Quality work isn't negotiable. We take pride in what we build, sweat the details that most people won't notice, and stand behind every single project we complete and deliver.

Many of our clients return for additional projects or refer family and friends. That repeat trust is the best measure of our success, and we work hard to earn it every single time.

A condo primary bath in Braintree, rebuilt from the studs with a rift oak vanity, freestanding tub, and walk-in glass shower.

This Braintree primary bath was rebuilt from the studs in a condo, where the toilet and shower had been closed off in a separate room. Opening that wall turned two tight spaces into one continuous bath.

A floating double vanity in rift sawn white oak, from the Tedd Wood line, anchors the room. It pairs with Arctic White quartz, two undermount sinks, and brushed nickel Riobel faucets. The back wall carries a dark botanical wallpaper behind two LED mirrors, with a rift oak panel running across the soffit above. A matching oak linen tower adds full-height storage.

The walk-in shower is finished in marble-look tile with a pebble stone floor, a built-in bench, and a niche with shelves. A freestanding Maax tub sits along the tiled wall with a wall-mounted filler.

A Marshfield family wanted a brighter kitchen, so we reworked the entire first floor to get it.

This Marshfield family wanted more natural light in their kitchen. The way to get it was not a bigger window alone. It was rethinking the whole first floor. The old pantry and laundry sat exactly where the light needed to come in, so we moved them into a new addition off the back of the house. That freed up room to grow the kitchen and made space for a large window over the sink, with the backyard and the trees now in view while you work.

Opened to the great room. We took down the wall between the kitchen and the two-story great room and set a beam in its place, so the two spaces read as one. The kitchen borrows light and height from the room next door, and the family can cook, eat, and gather without walls between them.

A backsplash that anchors the room. Behind the cooktop, a single slab of granite runs the full height of the wall. Its gold and charcoal veining sits against high-gloss white cabinetry and warm bamboo, and it is the piece your eye finds the moment you walk in.

WHY A WHOLE-FLOOR REMODEL

A first floor that finally flows.

Most homes we walk into have been remodeled piece by piece over the years, a kitchen one decade, a bath the next. A first floor remodel is the chance to start fresh, with every space designed to work with the next.

One Cohesive Design

Cabinetry, trim, flooring, and finishes that carry across every room, because they were designed together from day one.

One Team, Start to Finish

Your designer and project manager stay with you from the first sketch to the final walkthrough. No handoffs, no dropped details.

Done Once, Done Right

Doing it all at once means less disruption, better pricing on overlapping trades, and a home you won't need to renovate again.

WHAT'S INCLUDED

What a first floor remodel covers.

No two projects are the same. Some start with a kitchen and grow from there. Others reimagine the whole main level at once. We'll walk your home with you, listen to how you live in it, and help you decide what stays, what changes, and how it all fits together.

Kitchens
Custom cabinetry, countertops, and layout, plus every detail in between
Bathrooms and powder rooms

Living and dining areas
Opened up, reconnected, and unified with matching trim and finishes
Mudrooms, pantries, and laundry
The workhorse spaces that make a first floor actually function
Fireplaces and built-ins
Custom carpentry that turns architectural features into focal points
Structural work
Walls removed or added, beams installed, openings reframed
Flooring, lighting, and finishes
Continuous across the whole floor for a cohesive, finished feel

WHY A WHOLE-FLOOR REMODEL

Two paths to the same result.

Every home is different, and so is every remodel. The goal is always the same, a first floor that finally works the way you live. How we get there depends on your home, your goals, and what the design calls for.

WITHIN THE FOOTPRINT
Rethinking the space you have.
Walls come down, rooms reconnect, and the first floor starts to breathe. For most homes, this is all it takes. The bones were good. The layout was just working against you.
EXPANDING THE FOOTPRINT
When a little more room is the answer.
Sometimes the best design needs a bit more square footage, a kitchen bump-out, a first-floor primary suite, a bigger mudroom. When that's the case, we handle it as part of the larger remodel, with the same team, the same schedule, and the same care.

THE DESIGN-BUILD DIFFERENCE

Built by the team that designed it.

A first floor remodel has a lot of moving parts. Cabinetry, millwork, flooring, tile, lighting, plumbing, electrical, framing, all connecting across multiple rooms. One detail off, and you can feel it.

That's why we keep design and construction under one roof. One team is accountable for the whole project, from the first sketch to the final walkthrough. No handoffs. No finger-pointing. Just a home that came out the way it was supposed to.
